name: Full-Body Kettlebell Circuit — Pass / Lunge Drive / Snatch / Press-March
description: A four-move full-body kettlebell circuit: around-the-body pass to squat, reverse lunge to knee drive, snatch, and single-arm press to march, run in sequence for 3 rounds. Low-and-explosive conditioning on a single bell — a close sibling to the Asgooch cardio complex (row/clean/squat/snatch), same full-body conditioning intent with a snatch as the centerpiece. Round count is not stated in the source; 3 is the conventional read.

sets.name: Full-Body KB Circuit

exercises.notes: Pass around the body once → squat → next pass. Torso tall and still during the pass; full depth on the squat. Alternate pass direction.
Step back to a reverse lunge → drive the back knee forward and up to a tall, balanced stand → repeat. Drive through the front heel; stay tall.
Hips drive the bell, punch the hand THROUGH at the top for a soft catch — no bang on the wrist. Right shoulder watch on the catch; sub high pulls if it crackles.
Press with the shoulder packed DOWN, lock it out, then march alternate knees keeping the bell stacked overhead. Obliques fight to keep the torso square under the offset load.

sets.notes: Move through the four in order with minimal rest between moves. Rest ~60s between rounds, 3 rounds total. Light-to-moderate bell — this is conditioning, keep the breathing rate up. Source overlays read x20 / x10 / x10 / x10; the unilateral moves are written as per-side, scale to total if that's too much.

tips: Single bell throughout. Conditioning intent — pick a load you can keep moving with for 3 rounds, not a 1-rep-max bell.
The snatch is the technical centerpiece: hip drive, punch-through, soft catch. If the right shoulder complains, swap snatches for high pulls.

Sibling to the Asgooch cardio complex — same low-and-explosive full-body conditioning. Good fit for a Tuesday strength/conditioning rotation or a Saturday cardio choice; NOT for Thursday (no brutal/explosive finishing before Friday legs).
